newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels say army puts hostages at risk.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels say army puts hostages at risk.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas warned on Tuesday that the lives of the 60 Colombian soldiers they were holding prisoner were endangered by military operations.

In a communique issued by their international front in Mexico, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) also said they would not release the soldiers, captured in southern Putumayo Province on Aug. 30, anytime soon.

"The military operations not only make the prompt handover of the prisoners mentioned in our first communique of Sept. 4 impossible, but they also put their physical well-being in grave danger," the communique said.

It did not elaborate on the nature of the army operations, but Interior Minister Horacio Serpa responded by saying the government "offers all guarantees for the prompt release of the kidnapped soliders."
Serpa fell short of saying that the government would bow to rebel demands for the demilitarization of the parts of Putumayo Province where the soldiers were seized.

FARC rebels seized at least 60 soldiers and killed 27 people when they overran a jungle base in Las Delicias, Putumayo on Aug. 30. The attack started what authorities have described as the bloodiest guerrilla offensive in recent memory.
